Typed authoring owns only one literal import or export subcommand plus ordered arguments and emits exactly one compiler POSIX-quoted `sqoop` command with localParams=[]; it rejects controls, surrogates, DolphinScheduler placeholders, inline --password/--password= values, interactive -P, parameters, resources, output, and future fields. Native TEMPLATE and arbitrary CUSTOM scripts remain explicit selector-restricted opaque create/edit, while richer state is unchanged/export opaque preservation. Eligible workers require a POSIX shell, Sqoop, Hadoop/YARN, JDBC drivers, tenant execution permission, endpoint connectivity, credentials, and data access. This review refreshes no live evidence and promotes no profile.

DATAX.evidence: Exact per-version DataxParameters, DataxTask, task command execution plumbing, UI authoring, and regression sources prove one closed literal customConfig=1 JSON-object job envelope. KUBEFLOW.evidence: Exact 3.4.3 source closure review: Exact 3.2.0 through 3.4.3 Kubeflow parameter, executor, helper, registration, master-context, parameter-curing, UI, fixture, and official documentation sources prove one closed KUBEFLOW/tfjob_manifest subset. Canonical authoring owns a literal cluster name, Kubernetes namespace, and one ASCII LF YAML document whose only resource is apiVersion kubeflow.org/v1, kind TFJob, with metadata.namespace equal to the canonical namespace and metadata.name ending in the sole ${system.workflow.instance.id} placeholder. Every reviewed failover path may create a new task instance id while preserving workflowInstanceId and the appLink sentinel; the workflow-instance suffix therefore keeps kubectl apply/get/delete on one stable resource across failover while ordinary new executions get distinct identities; REPEAT_RUNNING reuses the original workflow instance id. The root requires nonempty spec.tfReplicaSpecs and excludes status, generateName, and server-owned metadata. Anchors, aliases, duplicate keys, YAML tags outside the JSON-core string/null/bool/int/float subset, including timestamp, binary, set, and custom tags, multiple documents/resources, other placeholders, parameters, resources, and richer or future fields are excluded. Deterministic REST projection emits only preserved yamlContent and compact legacy namespace JSON containing exactly name and cluster; decode strips only exact empty localParams/resourceList UI residue, while nonempty residue remains opaque. KubeflowTask performs raw prepared-value substitution before writing yamlContent and kubeconfig with the platform-default charset, so ASCII and the single built-in placeholder are deliberate portability and injection boundaries. It INFO-logs full task params, expanded manifest, kubectl commands, and results; every exact worker also exposes resolved kubeconfig in an INFO worker event, including where later task-log filtering applies; fields are not secret storage. KubeflowHelper runs kubectl apply, polls kubectl get -o json, and deletes via the same manifest. Tracking recognizes only Succeeded, Available, or Bound as success and Failed as failure for valid status shapes. Missing status or conditions and other nonterminal states can continue polling to the task timeout, but a present empty status.conditions array makes the helper dereference a missing last element and causes a runtime failure instead of continuing to poll; a compatible TFJob controller, kubectl, kubeconfig current context, CRDs, RBAC, network access, and an eventually terminal single-resource status are prerequisites. The stored appIds value is only an already-submitted sentinel, not a durable Kubeflow application id: after callback persistence AbstractRemoteTask can skip re-apply and resume polling after failover, but apply can succeed before the callback. Native retry does not guarantee a fresh training run: exact 3.2.x re-applies the same named TFJob, while 3.3.1 and newer copy the sentinel and only re-observe it. Workflow-instance REPEAT_RUNNING likewise reuses the original workflowInstanceId and resource name, so it may only re-observe old terminal state and is not a supported request for fresh training; a fresh execution must create a new workflow instance. dsctl therefore rejects workflow-instance rerun, recover-failed, and execute-task whenever available instance dagData reveals KUBEFLOW and directs fresh work to workflow run; direct UI or REST controls remain outside this guard. Typed workflow compilation therefore requires retry.times=0, a positive timeout in minutes with FAILED or WARNFAILED, a unique cluster/namespace/metadata.name template identity for each typed KUBEFLOW task in one workflow, and no authored workflow-global shadow of system.workflow.instance.id; project, startup-command, and inherited varPool shadowing remain runtime prerequisites. This closes only DolphinScheduler task retry; TFJob controller and pod restartPolicy behavior can still repeat work.
